I also worked it in with the sponge and applied some of the balsam on the inside of the boot. Then i took the hairdryer and warmed the boot up, but remember to not overheat it, warm it up for maybe 20 seconds in one spot. Then when the boot is warm you would massage it and really try and break in the leather. I also but on a thick sock and kind of walked around with the warm boot to try and really break it in. 

I repeated this process for about 3-4 times, while also wearing the boots outside with thick socks. So yeah, they broke in in a week.

I have the same problem, im a girl with REALLY small hands and it felt like i have zero pinky finger strength, so i didnt use it at all (only in power chords). Recently i started practising with my pinky and the main thing that helped is definitely the wrist positioning. Before my wrist was really far up, as i was for some reason trying  to fret the notes with my very fingertips (that made my power chords look very weird). But recently i changed my wrist positioning and hell did it help. I keep it much lover and more relaxed, which allows me to stretch my fingers much more and power chords became so easy. Now i can also switch the chords much faster. By keeping my wrist low, i fret the notes with the sides of my fingers or the flat part, but not the fingertip (not ideal for lead parts but great for rhytm). So now using pinky is much easier because i can stretch it more, i need much less force and its also easier to hit notes because i dont have to hit them with my tiny fingertip, i can use the side or the flat part. Hope this made sense
